correctness.rationale: All parameters s≠√n are excluded by exact one-coordinate norms. At n=2 and n=4 the complete unit-ball vertex sets are preserved by any real Hadamard matrix. For any three Hadamard columns in n≥8, orthogonality gives each of four pairwise sign patterns exactly n/4 times; the exhibited vector has transformed norm 3/2 and original norm max(1,3/√n)<3/2. Independent finite diagnostics cover all vertices at n=2,4 and every triple in Sylvester orders 8,16,32, without claiming finite proof of the universal case.

value.rationale: The family of cube–crosspolytope intersection balls is natural, and it is meaningful to determine whether real Hadamard orthogonality can become a genuine isometry of a non-Euclidean absolute symmetric Banach norm. The theorem classifies every Hadamard order and every continuous parameter, identifies the exceptional regular octagon and 24-cell, and supplies a fixed higher-dimensional distortion gap via triple-column sign combinatorics. It is not merely the already-known symmetry of the two low-dimensional polytopes.
